MOTIVES OF MURDER: 8.1 Out of the 9 specified motives, ‘Personal Vendetta or Enmity’ and ‘Property Dispute’ were the chief causes of murder followed by ‘Gain’, ‘Love intrigues’ and ‘Dowry’. These 5 causes together accounted for nearly 46 per cent of the total murders. The remaining 4 specified motives, namely: ‘Lunacy’, ‘Communalism’, ‘Casteism’ and ‘Class Conflict’ could explain only 2.9 per cent of murder cases. 51.1 per cent cases are not covered under any of the specified motives mentioned above and, thus, are categorized as ‘Other Motives’. While the collective share of all the chief causes of murder has decreased in 1992, compared to the previous year, the share of ‘Dowry’ as a motive of murder has increased significantly.
